title: GenWave Catalog Index
description: The committed index.json shape (SPEC F89.2) a GenWave station fetches directly from the repo root — built from entries/ by tools/build_index.py, and re-verified byte-for-byte plus schema-validated on every CI run (PR and push to main). additionalProperties is false throughout: this document is entirely catalog-tooling output, so an unrecognized field is a build regression worth failing CI on, not a forward-compat concern. Widened to the avatar and icon kinds, plus a persona entry's own optional avatar-sidecar `assets[]`, by SPEC F128.1/F128.2/F130.6 (PLAN T309).
$comment: Every pattern below ends in (?![\s\S]), a lookahead meaning 'no character follows' — a portable absolute-end-of-string anchor that means the same thing in Python re, ECMA-262 (the dialect JSON Schema nominally specifies, and what ajv/most other validators use), and .NET. Plain $ was rejected: in Python's re (which is what actually enforces this schema server-side, via the jsonschema library), $ also matches immediately before a trailing newline, so a value with a stray trailing \n would slip through. \Z was also tried and rejected: it's Python-only — under ECMA-262, \Z is a literal 'Z' character (Annex B identity escape), so a \Z-anchored pattern would reject every legitimate value and only accept ones ending in a literal Z. (?![\s\S]) has neither problem in any of the three dialects.

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD): the max `added` date across included entries' meta.json, or 1970-01-01 when the catalog has zero included entries (tools/build_index.py). Derived entirely from the tree, never from git history or wall-clock time.

entries.description: Sorted by slug. Never includes the example-dj documentation entry.

swatchSet.description: The five shelf-chip swatches for one mode (mirrors schemas/theme-meta.schema.json's own `swatchSet`).

assetRef.description: One binary asset (SPEC F104.1/F128.1/F128.2) — a font pack's woff2 face or OFL licence text, an avatar pack's PNG item, OR a persona entry's own optional `<slug>.avatar.png` sidecar face — sitting alongside (never inside) its own manifest. Mirrors GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator's own asset-ref shape: a closed per-kind path/extension alternation (no further path segment possible, so no leading slash/../URL scheme either) and a positive byte count bounded by the app's own fetch-transport size cap. The `bytes` ceiling below is deliberately the WIDER of the app's two per-kind ceilings (font: 256 KiB, GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogProxyService.MaxAssetBytes; avatar/persona-sidecar PNG: 512 KiB, GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.MaxPngAssetBytes) rather than one asymmetric bound per kind — tools/validate.py's own validate_font_pack (200 KiB summed pack ceiling) and validate_avatar_pack (512 KiB per item) already hold every REAL entry to its own tighter number, and tools/build_index.py always recomputes `bytes` from the file actually on disk, never a manifest's declared claim, so this schema-level ceiling is a defensive outer bound, not the operative one.

path.description: Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<kind-folder>/<slug>/ (the fixed kind folder every asset lives under, gh-33) — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own three-way alternation rules all three out for every branch. A font/avatar pack asset's filename is the pack's OWN free-chosen file name (e.g. "space-grotesk-variable-latin.woff2", "warm-grin.png") — constrained on character set and extension only, the same closed sets GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.FontAssetFileNameText/AvatarAssetFileNameText enforce app-side. A PERSONA entry's own sidecar face is SHAPE-ONLY here too (a slug-shaped `<anything>.avatar.png` under a slug-shaped directory, not literally the SAME slug as the directory) — draft-07 JSON Schema, this file's own dialect, has no way to express 'this path segment must equal a sibling property's value' that holds up across every consumer of the published schema. A prior revision of this pattern tried to pin that equality anyway with a Python `re`-only named-group backreference (`(?P<personaSlug>...)` / `(?P=personaSlug)`), wrongly citing this file's own top-level $comment — which documents `(?![\s\S])`'s PORTABILITY across ECMA-262/.NET/Python re — as precedent for a construct that is the opposite of portable: a backreference that FAILS TO COMPILE under ECMA-262 (ajv) and .NET, breaking the whole published schema for every non-Python consumer. Slug equality between a persona entry's own directory and its sidecar face's filename is instead enforced Python-side, in tools/validate.py's `validate_index_slug_ownership` (which already walks every entry's own `assets[]` against that entry's own `slug` for the ownership-prefix check immediately below) — the correct home for a cross-property constraint no dialect-portable JSON Schema pattern can express, mirroring GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.PersonaAvatarAssetPathPattern's own same-slug rule at the app's own layer instead of at this one.

bytes.description: Declared byte size of this asset. Bounded 1-524288 (512 KiB) — see this definition's own remarks for why this is the WIDER of the app's two per-kind ceilings rather than a tighter one split per branch; an asset declaring more than even the widest kind's own ceiling is malformed by definition regardless of which kind it belongs to.

entry.description: `card`/`manifest` (and, for kind:"font"/"avatar", `assets`) are conditionally required, not all listed here — see the `if`/`then`/`else` below, gated on `kind`. A persona entry's own `assets` (SPEC F128.2) is the one exception: it's OPTIONAL even for that kind, never required — see the final `else` branch's own remarks.

kind.description: Entry discriminator (SPEC F103.2 / T178, widened to "font" by F104.1 / T195, widened to "show" by F118.1 / T253, widened to "avatar" and "icon" by F128.1/F130.6 / T309). Optional — an entry with no `kind` is treated as "persona", matching every pre-F103.2 entry and the app's own back-compat default (GenWave.Host, T176: a missing `kind` defaults to persona; an unrecognized `kind` value there causes the app to skip just that one entry, not abort the whole index — this schema is stricter than the app and rejects an unrecognized value outright, since here it can only mean a build regression in this repo's own tooling, not a newer app talking to an older catalog). `kind` decides which file-ref property below is required and which path pattern its `path` must match: "persona" (or omitted) requires `card` matching `*.persona.json` — the unchanged, pre-F103.2 shape, and MAY additionally carry a single-element `assets` (its own optional avatar sidecar, SPEC F128.2); "theme" requires `manifest` matching `*.theme.json`; "font" requires BOTH `manifest` matching `*.font.json` AND a non-empty `assets` array (SPEC F104.1 — a font entry is `{manifest, meta}` plus its vendored asset files, the first binary files in the catalog); "show" requires `manifest` matching `*.show.json` (SPEC F118.1 — a show entry is `{manifest, meta}` with no assets, family, or preview, the same minimal shape as a theme entry minus its swatch preview); "avatar" requires BOTH `manifest` matching `*.avatar.json` AND a non-empty `assets` array (SPEC F128.1 — the same pack-shaped, all-or-nothing posture as "font", minus a `family` equivalent); "icon" requires `manifest` matching `*.icon.json` (SPEC F130.6 — the same minimal `{manifest, meta}` shape as "show": licence/provenance live only in meta.json).

preview.description: Projected from a kind:"theme" entry's meta.json (T191, mirrors the `bestFor` precedent above) — the shelf-card swatch contract (T185): a HANDFUL of key token hex values per mode, enough to paint shelf chips without fetching and parsing the full manifest. Only ever present on a kind:"theme" entry; a persona entry's meta.json carries no `preview` field, so build_index.py never stamps this key onto one. Excluded from a kind:"font" entry too (T195 review N8) and a kind:"show" entry too (T253) — the font and show `then` branches' own `allOf` each reject an entry of that kind carrying this key, the same posture the theme branch already takes on `assets`/`family`: neither a font pack nor a show has a swatch preview to project, T191's projection is theme-only. Definitions duplicated from schemas/theme-meta.schema.json rather than $ref'd across files, the same standalone-file posture that schema's own $comment documents for its `added` pattern.

path.description: Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/personas/<slug>/ (the fixed kind folder every persona entry lives under, gh-33) — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out.

Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<kind-folder>/<slug>/ to the kind:"theme", kind:"font", kind:"show", kind:"avatar", or kind:"icon" manifest file (SPEC F103.2 / F104.1 / F118.1 / F128.1 / F130.6) — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out. The kind-folder segment is the six-way alternation (personas|themes|fonts|shows|avatars|icons, gh-33/T309) since this definition is shared kind-blind — the SPECIFIC folder a given kind actually lives under (themes/ for a theme entry, and so on) is pinned by the `manifest.path` pattern nested in each `if`/`then`/`else` branch below instead, same posture as the extension. The exact required extension (`*.theme.json` for a theme entry, `*.font.json` for a font entry, `*.show.json` for a show entry, `*.avatar.json` for an avatar entry, `*.icon.json` for an icon entry) is likewise deliberately NOT enforced here — it's pinned per-kind by that same nested pattern, so a theme entry naming a `.font.json` manifest (or vice versa) fails there rather than validating against this shared, kind-blind definition (a prior version of this pattern accepted either extension regardless of `kind`, letting the two cross-dress). The one `manifest` key every non-persona kind targets (F103.2's generalised `{manifest, meta}` model); persona entries keep using `card` (see the `kind` description above) rather than this key — and, as of the persona `else` branch's own `allOf` (T195 review N7), are schema-rejected from carrying this key at all: an entry with no `kind` (or `kind: "persona"`) that names both `card` and `manifest` validated clean before that addition even though it's a shape GenWave.Host's own kind resolution never produces and would reject the whole index over app-side (exactly one of `card`/`manifest` is ever expected, never both).

assets.description: A kind:"font" or kind:"avatar" entry's own vendored asset files (SPEC F104.1/F128.1) — a font pack's 1-2 latin-subsetted woff2 faces plus its OFL licence text, OR an avatar pack's PNG items — each carrying `path`/`sha256`/`bytes`. ALSO, separately (SPEC F128.2), a PERSONA entry's own OPTIONAL single-element `assets` — its `<slug>.avatar.png` sidecar face; unlike the pack-shaped kinds' all-or-nothing posture, this key is never REQUIRED on a persona entry, and when present is capped to exactly one element by the persona `else` branch's own override below. Theme/show/icon entries carry no `assets` key at all. minItems 1 mirrors GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator's own "zero assets" rejection (TryValidateAssets) — this schema is at least as strict, rejecting an empty array at CI time rather than only at app fetch time. uniqueItems (T196) is full-object uniqueness (path/sha256/bytes all equal, not just a duplicate `path`) — an entry's own assets[] should never carry the same asset twice, the same posture files[]'s own duplicate-asset gate already takes one layer down in a font pack's own manifest (tools/validate.py's font-duplicate-asset check). Because draft-07 has no way to pin uniqueness on a single property alone, uniqueItems does NOT by itself catch two assets sharing the same `path` with a DIFFERENT `sha256`/`bytes` — the app dedupes an entry's assets on `path` ALONE (CatalogIndexValidator.TryValidateAssets again), so that pair would silently lose one asset app-side even though it passes this schema untouched. tools/validate.py's validate_index_duplicate_asset_paths (T196 review M2) is the actual gate against that case, the same Python-side cross-property posture validate_index_slug_ownership already takes for path ownership.

family.description: The OPTIONAL shelf-card family name projected onto a kind:"font" entry (STORY-281 AC1, T195/T196 — copied from the pack's own manifest `family` by tools/build_index.py so a zero-fetch shelf listing can show it without fetching `.font.json`). Shape and length mirror GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.FamilyPattern/MaxFamilyLength exactly — the same CSS-injection-safe character set (and 64-character cap) ThemeManifestParser.FontFamilyPattern enforces on a theme manifest's own font family, since this value reaches the wire (and an inline CSS `style`/`font-family` value) the same way a theme's shelf preview swatches do.

path.description: Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<kind-folder>/<slug>/ — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out. Every kind carries a meta.json, so unlike `card`/`manifest` above this definition stays kind-blind at the folder segment too — the six-way alternation (personas|themes|fonts|shows|avatars|icons, gh-33/T309), never narrowed to one specific folder by an `if`/`then`/`else` branch below.

bytes.description: A font entry's own assets[] items are held to the NARROWER 262144-byte (256 KiB) ceiling — GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogProxyService.MaxAssetBytes, the real per-face fetch-transport cap for the font kind — rather than the shared `assetRef` definition's own wider 524288-byte (512 KiB) bound. That wider bound exists ONLY to also admit the avatar/persona-sidecar PNG kind's own real 512 KiB ceiling (GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.MaxPngAssetBytes); left unnarrowed here, a font entry's own assets[] would validate up to 512 KiB even though the app rejects anything over 256 KiB the moment it tries to fetch a font face — restores 'this schema is at least as strict as the app' for the font kind specifically, rather than only at the shared definition's own widest-of-both-kinds level.

assets.description: A persona entry's own assets[], when present, is capped to exactly one element (SPEC F128.2: "at most one") — narrower than the shared `assets` definition's own minItems:1 alone. Unlike kind:"font"/kind:"avatar" above, this key stays OPTIONAL here (no `required` entry for it): absent means no worn face, the ordinary pre-F128 shape.
